The test image shows a tomato leaf with:
- Extensive marginal/tip necrosis (brown to dark brown/black), especially on the left lobe
- Yellowing (chlorosis) in transition zones between necrotic and green tissue
- No concentric ring patterns (rules out Early Blight)
- No small specks or spots (rules out Septoria, Bacterial Speck)
- No white powdery coating (rules out Powdery Mildew)

The pattern of large dark brown-to-black marginal lesions with a greasy-dark appearance is most consistent with Late Blight. I'll use my one reference view to confirm.

The Late Blight reference shows large, irregular dark brown necrotic lesions spreading across leaf surfaces — similar texture and coloration to the test image. The test image shows the same characteristic pattern: extensive dark brown/black necrosis at the margins and tip of a tomato leaf, with a yellowing transition zone toward the still-green central tissue. No concentric rings, no spots, no powdery coating — consistent with Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans).
